title: Effect of Sintering Parameters on the Microstructural Properties of Nanostructured Inconel 718
content: Inconel 718 (IN718) superalloy is widely used owing to its high oxidation resistance property and excellent mechanical performance at relatively high working temperatures. Its most notable applications include aerospace, aeroengine manufacturing, petrochemical industries, and nuclear power generation [1-2]. Several studies have investigated the influence of fabrication processes on superalloys as powder metallurgy route and it has been observed that some of the most significant results directly impact their performance. Additionally, sintering methods such as conventional sintering (C.S) and hot isostatic pressing (HIP) have been explored to develop alloys with enhanced homogeneity, finer, and denser microstructures, thereby improving their mechanical properties [2,3]. This research focuses on studying the effect of C.S. and different HIP compaction pressures due to their potential to induce significant microstructural changes, such as grain refinement and reduction in crystallite size, resulting in alloys with dense microstructures and superior mechanical behavior.
